discovery: The gauge/gravity (AdS/CFT) holographic duality between quantum gravity and quantum field theory

nominees.name: Juan Maldacena
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

nominees.name: Edward Witten
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

motivation: In 1997 Maldacena conjectured that string theory in anti-de Sitter space is exactly equivalent to a conformal gauge theory on its boundary. Polyakov (with Gubser and Klebanov) and Witten supplied the precise dictionary relating gravitational and field-theory observables. This made the holographic principle concrete and calculable. It gave the first non-perturbative definition of quantum gravity, in which black-hole evaporation is unitary. It also provided a tool for strongly coupled systems: the predicted near-minimal shear viscosity agrees with quark-gluon plasma data from RHIC and the LHC, and the duality now informs studies of strange metals and quantum chaos. Most profoundly, it revealed that spacetime geometry emerges from quantum entanglement, which has reshaped quantum information science and gravity alike. Holography is one of the most consequential conceptual advances in fundamental physics in recent decades, and it has been tested by thousands of consistent, independent calculations.
